prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: I keep B011 as a single-part prize with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The round-1 exchange did not touch the core scientific claim: nobody disputes that a bifunctional molecule can recruit an E3 ligase to a chosen protein and have it destroyed, that this has been reproduced by many groups, and that it opens targets without an active site. That is the kind of simple, completely new principle with visible consequences that I mean by a game-changer. What persuades me most, as a theorist, is that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures and cooperativity analysis turned a clever idea into quantitative design rules. Crews and Deshaies hold the concept and first proof of principle; Ciulli holds the part that made it rational and transferable. I do not count the four B011 supporters as an argument; the argument is that the principle is sound, general and already used as a research tool well beyond pharmacology.
statement.case_against: The reservations stand and I have not removed them. No degrader is a broadly approved drug, and I cannot verify trial outcomes myself, so a prize now rests on mechanism and tool value more than on proven medicines. Credit is crowded: Sakamoto and Kim are left out of the founding paper, and the cereblon and molecular-glue lineage of Handa, Ito and Gray is a distinct strand that a citation about degradation will be read as covering. Choosing three names means defending those omissions openly. If the committee judged the clinical case essential, I would expect it to wait.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Handa in the trio in place of Ciulli and words the citation to cover molecular glues, so that the cereblon mechanism behind thalidomide-class drugs is recognised.
responses.response: The chair's question is the right one and I have thought about it again. Cereblon is a striking mechanistic result, but it explains drugs found by other routes, while the prize I would defend rests on a design principle that others can apply to any protein. A trio with Handa and without Ciulli would leave the rational ternary-complex work unrecognised, and Handa alone cannot stand for the glue strand, since Ito and Gray would still be outside. I would accept a citation phrase that is wide enough not to exclude glues, but I would not give up Ciulli. If the committee wants the glue strand to be explicitly honoured, that is a reason to wait for a later year, not to dilute this one.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B058 (Gray and Winkler) because the mechanism is physically stated, confirmed for four decades and has a clean two-name attribution, and he flags overlap with Marcus, Dutton and Moser.
responses.response: I respect the maturity argument and B058 is the one alternative whose experimental quality I do not doubt. Our difference is in what a prize adds now. Your own caveat, that Marcus theory and the empirical distance relations of Dutton and Moser sit next to it, means that the citation would have to be written narrowly around the demonstration in proteins, and that is a contestable line. I would rank B058 clearly above B055 on science, but behind B011 on novelty of consequences. I ask you directly whether you would move to B011 if B058 cannot reach five votes, since your round-1 file already lists it as an alternative.

responses.point: Somfai holds B055 for its daily use, thirty years of confirmation and clean Buchwald and Hartwig credit, while admitting the 2010 prize and the Kosugi antecedent.
responses.response: I agree that B055 has the best-defined attribution and no maturity risk, and I would not call it undeserving. My concern is the chair's question about Kosugi and the 2010 cross-coupling prize: if the committee feels the principle was already honoured, the citation becomes a prize for an important extension, which is a lower bar than I want to apply. Your uncertainty list says you would need to decide how hard to hold if B011 attracts a majority. I think the scientific points above are a fair basis for that decision, and I do not ask you to move on the strength of vote counts.

responses.point: Zou argues that B005 (Grätzel and O'Regan) is the only candidate whose recognition is clearly overdue, with sharp credit, but concedes perovskites have overtaken the practical impact and Hagfeldt may be required.
responses.response: The 1991 cell is a real conceptual ancestor of hybrid photovoltaics and I find the overdue argument fair. Where I hesitate is the standard of consequences: you yourself state that practical impact was overtaken, and the Hagfeldt question would push the list to three names and weaken the claim of clean credit. I would put B005 below B011 for those reasons, though not far below. The two-name attribution is a genuine advantage that B011 does not share.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will centre the prize on PROTACs or also on molecular glues and cereblon, which changes the third laureate between Ciulli and Handa
Whether clinical validation of degraders is sufficient, which I cannot verify independently
Whether Sakamoto and Kim can be left out and the omission defended in public
Whether the members with other first choices will accept B011 as a single-part prize if their own preference cannot reach five votes
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. I have no personal or institutional tie to the degrader candidates. As a computational chemist and former Warshel postdoc, I remain aware of a possible bias toward simulation work (B053), which is only an alternative here. No recusal is needed.
